meta.title: Land Kit AI Integration Guide
meta.description: How to access and use Land Kit AI reference documentation for comprehensive landscape design workflows
meta.scope: Land Kit is a broad toolkit for landscape design and analysis - plants, paving, grading, environmental analysis, cost estimation, visualization, and more

quick_start.for_raven: If you're using Raven in Grasshopper, reference Land Kit docs to generate scripts for any landscape design task
quick_start.for_developers: If you're building a Grasshopper AI tool, integrate Land Kit documentation to enable intelligent component chaining
quick_start.for_users: If you want to generate Land Kit scripts with AI, describe what you're designing - plants, paving, grading, analysis, or combinations

what_is_land_kit.overview: Land Kit is a comprehensive landscape design toolkit with 125+ components across multiple domains

domains.name: Plant Design
domains.description: Niche-based plant placement, constraint solving, species selection, bloom calendars, plant schedules
domains.example: Fill a garden with plants that fit site conditions (sun, soil, water)

domains.name: Paving & Patterns
domains.description: Tessellations, color patterns, custom paver layouts, rationalization, textured surfaces
domains.example: Create a paving pattern with color gradients across an area

domains.name: Site Grading
domains.description: Topographic modifications, slope analysis, stairs, walls, fill/cut analysis, terracing
domains.example: Create graded terraces with custom slopes and walls

domains.name: Environmental Analysis
domains.description: Hydrology (catchments, flow), soil infiltration (CN), solar exposure, temperature, cost, carbon
domains.example: Calculate watershed runoff and infiltration for drainage design

domains.name: Area & Slab Design
domains.description: Create, modify, and analyze landscape areas - surfaces, slabs, meshes, clipping, collaging
domains.example: Design overlapping planting areas with different plant mixes

domains.name: Output & Visualization
domains.description: Drawings, schedules, CAD export, baking, labeling, mesh generation
domains.example: Generate a plant schedule with blooming calendars and cost estimates

Example workflows across different domains - reference proven patterns

usage_scenarios.scenario: I want to design a planting layout with constrained placement
steps: 1. Ask AI: 'Design a planting layout where plants fit available sun and soil conditions'
2. AI fetches component_connections.json to understand Plant workflow components
3. AI references component_registry.json for constraint options
4. AI generates script using Niche selection and constraint-based placement
usage_scenarios.prompt_example: Create a Grasshopper script that places plants in areas based on niche constraints (sun exposure 3-6 hrs, soil moisture medium). Show a plant schedule output.

usage_scenarios.scenario: I want to create paving with color patterns and optimize the pattern
steps: 1. Ask AI: 'Create tessellation pattern with color gradients, then rationalize it'
2. AI finds pattern components and rationalization components via connections map
3. AI chains components: Tessellation → Color Rule → Rationalize Pattern
4. AI generates integrated workflow
usage_scenarios.prompt_example: Generate a paving pattern using tessellations with a gradient color scheme. Rationalize the result to minimize paver types.

usage_scenarios.scenario: I want multi-domain site analysis - environmental + cost
steps: 1. Ask AI: 'Analyze site for hydrology AND calculate carbon/cost'
2. AI queries component_connections.json for analysis pathways
3. AI sees Environment layers feed both hydro and cost analyses
4. AI creates parallel workflows that share environment setup
usage_scenarios.prompt_example: Create environment analysis for both stormwater runoff (CN calculation) and landscaping carbon footprint. Show results separately.

usage_scenarios.scenario: I want to grade terrain with custom slopes and add walls
steps: 1. Ask AI: 'Grade topography with variable slopes, add walls at edges'
2. AI finds Topo modification and wall components
3. AI chains: Elevation → Grade Topo Mod → Create Walls
4. AI generates grading script with wall integration
usage_scenarios.prompt_example: Create a script that modifies topo with custom slope values (2%, 5%, 8%) and adds retaining walls where slopes exceed 10%.

usage_scenarios.scenario: I want to combine plant design with visualization and schedules
steps: 1. Ask AI: 'Design plants AND generate schedule AND cost estimate'
2. AI chains: Plant layout → Get Plant Info → Draw Plant Schedule → Calculate costs
3. AI knows data flows through component_connections.json
4. AI creates multi-output workflow
usage_scenarios.prompt_example: Create a landscape design with plant placement, then output a plant schedule, bloom calendar, and cost breakdown.

example_user_prompts.description: Real-world prompts users can send to Raven or other AI tools, referencing the Land Kit documentation
example_user_prompts.how_to_use: Copy these patterns and adapt them to your specific needs. Always include the manifest URL so the AI has access to current documentation.

examples.prompt: I want to build a Grasshopper script using Land Kit components to do the grading using the info I have in this file. Here is the Land Kit documentation: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chrislandau/land-kit-docs/main/ai-reference/manifest.json

Create a planting script using Land Kit that selects plants based on available sun (4-6 hours), soil type (loam), and water availability. Reference: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chrislandau/land-kit-docs/main/ai-reference/manifest.json

Generate a tessellating paving pattern with color gradients using Land Kit components. Then rationalize it to minimize paver types. Documentation: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chrislandau/land-kit-docs/main/ai-reference/manifest.json

Build a script that calculates both stormwater runoff (using CN values) and landscaping carbon footprint. Reference the Land Kit docs: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chrislandau/land-kit-docs/main/ai-reference/manifest.json

Create a landscape design that combines plant selection with cost estimation, grading analysis, and a printable plant schedule. Use Land Kit: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chrislandau/land-kit-docs/main/ai-reference/manifest.json

how_to_prompt: Describe what you're designing: 'Design a perennial garden with...' or 'Create paving with...' or 'Analyze site hydrology for...'
Reference domains: 'Use plant design components' or 'Focus on grading modifications' or 'Do environmental analysis'
Ask for specific operations: 'Add tessellation patterns', 'Calculate cost estimates', 'Generate plant schedules'
Ask for validation: 'Check component compatibility' or 'Validate data types in my workflow'
Reference component types by category: 'Use all PATTERN components' or 'Connect ANALYSIS outputs to OUTPUT components'
key_tips: Land Kit has 125 components - Raven can combine them in novel ways based on data type compatibility
Use component_connections.json to understand what outputs feed what inputs
Many workflows are possible - describe the outcome you want, let AI find the path
You can layer multiple analyses on same environment (hydrology + solar + cost)
Custom layers can be created for any data type - not limited to predefined layers

recommended_load_order: 1. Load component_registry.json on startup (list all available components)

caching_strategy.approach: Download and cache on startup, check version field daily
caching_strategy.ttl: 24 hours for registry, 7 days for connections and patterns
caching_strategy.fallback: Include minimal local copies for offline mode

workflow_generation.approach: Use component_connections.json to route data types intelligently
benefits: Works across all Land Kit domains
workflow_generation.example: If output type=Plant and input accepts=Plant, those can connect. Same for any data type.

steps: When user reports error, check error_reference.json
Look up error ID or error message text
Provide solution from reference
Optionally regenerate script with fix
error_handling.note: Not all errors will be in reference; document new ones encountered
